chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his paternal uncle Yaʿqūb al-Aḥmar, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him about a woman who had been menstruating and then saw purification: may her husband have intercourse with her before she performs ghusl? He said: No, not until she performs ghusl.

He said: And I asked him about a woman who menstruated while traveling, then became pure, but did not find water for a day or two. Is it lawful for her husband to have intercourse with her before she performs ghusl? He said: It is not proper until she performs ghusl.

key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: cessation of menstruation and attainment of purity from bleeding
key_terms.طَامِثًا: a woman in the state of menstruation
key_terms.لَا يَصْلُحُ: it is not proper or not permitted in this context
key_terms.يُجَامِعَهَا: to have sexual intercourse with her

ai.seo_question: Can a husband have intercourse with his wife after her menstrual bleeding ends but before ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a husband may not have intercourse with his wife after the cessation of menstrual bleeding until she performs ghusl. It also addresses the case of travel and lack of water, maintaining the same ruling until ghusl is completed.
